newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk coalition prepares for military meeting.
newsitem.headline: Turk coalition prepares for military meeting.

text.p: Turkey's political and military leaders were set for a key meeting on Saturday amid a rising atmosphere of crisis in the Islamist-led coalition of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan.

The powerful National Security Council, chaired by President Suleyman Demirel, was scheduled to meet at 3 p.m. (1200 GMT) for talks expected to focus on military demands for an anti-Islamist crackdown.
Leading newspapers said Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller had warned Erbakan on Friday she would pull out of government unless his party agreed to the military requests.
"Going, going, gone," shouted a banner headline in the mass-circulation Hurriyet daily, predicting an end to the 10-month-old coalition.
"The ties are being cut," said a Yeni Yuzyil headline.
Talks were likely to deal with a key army demand, opposed by Erbakan's Welfare Party, that the state's secularist education be extended to eight years from five, media reports said.
The planned education reforms would marginalise religious secondary schools, the breeding ground of future Islamists.
Pro-Western conservative Ciller and Erbakan held almost two hours of hastily arranged talks on Friday evening. The two avoided the press after the meeting.
Ciller had earlier denied a press report that she would withdraw her True Path party from modern Turkey's first Islamist-led government.
